title: Exit Narrative Synthesis — Forensic Canvas
content:
PURPOSE:
A lightweight forensic canvas to synthesize why an account decided not to renew. Use this to produce a 3-minute exec summary, a detailed timeline of signals, prioritized root-cause hypotheses, counterfactual scenarios (what we could have done differently), and a short salvage/playbook runbook for future similar cases.

QUICK FACTS (one-pager):
- Account: {{account_name}}
- ARR at renewal: ${{arr}}
- Contract type: hosted / dedicated / private (pick)
- Primary contact: {{name}} (role)
- Renewal decision date: {{YYYY-MM-DD}}
- CS owner on renewal: {{owner}}
- Net churn reason (customer words): "{{customer_quote_short}}"
- Impact score: 1-10 (rev + strategic) -> {{impact_score}}

3-MINUTE EXEC SUMMARY (bullet list):
- Top-line reason: (e.g., "cost + missing integration")
- Most actionable root cause: (single sentence)
- Primary evidence supporting cause: (usage drop, email thread, billing dispute id)
- Immediate mitigation recommended: (e.g., short-term discount + integration sprint)

TIMELINE (anchor events — populate chronologically):
- T-minus 6 months: initial deployment / kickoff notes (link to kickoff playbook)
- T-minus 3 months: usage metrics trend (embed chart reference) -> key drop on {{date}}
- T-minus 2 months: escalation email from buyer: "{{snippet}}" (link)
- T-minus 1 month: renewal discussion notes (meeting id / recording)
- Decision date: customer says no — reason given: "{{full_quote}}"
- Post-decision follow-ups: credits/refund/closedown actions logged (ticket ids)

EVIDENCE BUCKETS (what to collect and attach):
- Product telemetry: DAU/MAU, API calls, error rates, tail latencies, model variant used, token costs per month (attach CSV or dashboard link)
- Financial: invoices, disputed charges, discount approvals, procurement delays (attach pdfs)
- Comms: meeting notes, Slack history, support tickets, email threads (link to thread IDs)
- Implementation: integration docs, migration tickets, professional services notes, backlog items postponed
- People: org chart, decision-maker changes, new stakeholder hired/fired

ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESES (prioritize 1-3):
- Hypothesis A (most likely): short label e.g., "Economics (unit cost exceeded ROI)"
  Evidence: bullet list (usage per seat, token spend spike, POC cost vs forecast)
  Gap that would disprove: e.g., "if finance confirms internal budget reallocation unrelated to product cost"
- Hypothesis B: e.g., "Missing integration with core platform"
  Evidence: backlog PRs, blocked tickets, vendor statements
  Gap that would disprove: "integration delivered on time and still churned"
- Hypothesis C: e.g., "Product quality / incorrect expectations"
  Evidence: support tickets, demo mismatches, evals failing
  Gap that would disprove: "customer reported positive NPS / feature satisfaction before exit"

COUNTERFACTUAL SCENARIOS (what would have changed the outcome):
- Counterfactual 1: "Offer 3-month cost shield and technical integration runway"
  Probability it would have saved renewal: high/medium/low -> justify
  Cost to us: credits, SE time, priority engineering slot
- Counterfactual 2: "Escalate to executive sponsor + procurement assistance"
  Probability and cost
- Counterfactual 3: "Roll back to smaller model/quantized variant to reduce cost"
  Probability and cost

SALVAGE PLAYBOOK (operational checklist we attempted / should attempt):
- Immediate outreach: executive sync within 48 hours -> owner: {{name}}, status: (done/pending)
- Finance concession: short-term credit or payment plan -> owner: {{name}}, amount: ${{amt}}, status
- Tactical engineering: 2-week integration sprint or hotfix -> ticket IDs, owner
- Offer a pilot extension with SLO guarantees -> terms drafted (link)
- If declined: closeout checklist (data retention, offboarding, feedback survey)

LEARNING AGENDA & ACTIONS (concrete, assign owners & due dates):
- Short-term (0-30 days): e.g., "Create a friction checklist for integrations and require gating at P0 for renewals" -> owner: Priya Desai -> due: 2024-11-01
- Medium (30-90 days): "Automate spend alerts for customers approaching X% of forecasted token budget" -> owner: Eng-product -> due
- Long (90+ days): "Revise renewal playbook to include cost-protection options and standard legal templates" -> owner: CS leadership

METRICS TO TRACK TO AVOID REPEAT (minimum viable signals to wire):
- Usage decline flag (20% month-over-month for 2 months)
- Token spend variance vs forecast ( > 30%)
- Support severity > P2 for > 7 days during pre-renewal window
- Integration backlog items unresolved at renewal

STAKEHOLDERS & CONTACTS (populate):
- Customer exec sponsor: {{name}} / email
- Procurement contact: {{name}} / email
- Internal: CS AE, Solutions Eng, Account Exec, Finance rep, Engineering lead

EVIDENCE APPENDIX (place links or paste snippets):
- Attach: dashboard links, export CSVs, meeting recording links, legal terms, PO requests

NOTES TO REVIEWER (raw):
- Known uncertainty areas: billing timeline ambiguous between Finance and customer procurement team. Flag: confirm invoice sent date with billing@redwood.
- Quick wins flagged during review: auto-notify customer 30 days before predicted token overrun (small effort)
- Hypothesis testing plan: run a 6-week cohort where we offer integrated onboarding and cost-guard for similar mid-market accounts; measure lift in renewal rate

TEMPLATE USAGE INSTRUCTIONS:
- Save a copy per lost account (naming: yyyy-mm-dd-account-exit-narrative.json)
- Attach evidence links and add line-level owners for each action when assigning to sprints
- Use the 3-minute exec summary section for QBR decks and postmortem distribution

SIGN-OFF:
- CS reviewer: ____________________  date: ______
- Product reviewer: _______________  date: ______
- SRE/Eng reviewer (if technical cause): ________ date: ______

END OF TEMPLATE

(Internal note: this canvas is intentionally concise so we can generate a repeatable dataset for QBR sharing and machine-readable hooks — keep evidence links short. Remove PII before sharing externally.)
